payload.body: The submediant is scale degree 6 of a key: the pitch a major sixth above the tonic in a major key and a minor sixth above the tonic in a natural minor key, bearing the submediant function as the subordinate degree of the scale's upper region. In C major the submediant is A (the root of the iv chord, an A-minor triad), and in A natural minor it is F (the root of the VI chord, an F-major triad). Parameters: (1) intervallic status — the submediant sits a major sixth above the tonic in major keys and a minor sixth above the tonic in natural minor keys; it is a whole step above the dominant and a third below the tonic (a minor third in major keys, a major third in natural minor keys). (2) functional role — it is the degree that commonly moves to the dominant as a pre-dominant or colour degree (submediant–dominant motion, iv–V or VI–V), and it names the key a third from the tonic (the vi / VI key, one of the keys in mediant relation to the tonic). (3) relational definition — the submediant is defined relative to the tonic (the submediant of C major is A; of A minor is F) and is the sixth ordinal of the key's scale. Persistence mechanism: codified in Western tonal and harmonic theory, taught in music-theory and harmony curricula (scale-degree numbering; Roman-numeral analysis naming iv in major and VI in minor), reproduced in composition and analysis practice (identifying the submediant's pre-dominant motion and its role in modulation to the related key), and maintained through the conventions of tonal notation. It is distinguished from the mediant (scale degree 3 — a third above the tonic, the lower of the two 'mediant' degrees; the submediant is a sixth, not a third), from the dominant (scale degree 5 — the point of greatest harmonic tension; the submediant sits a whole step above it and bears a subordinate, preparatory function rather than the tension function), and from a bare pitch (any point on the pitch axis; the submediant is a pitch bearing a specific ordinal and function). [formal: submediantia | substrate: mind | horizon: centuries | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]
